The switch decides

You picked A. Every picture below is shot out of a real build made from the sources with your rule in it — not a drawing of one.

“the custodian should have always access to their unit or function entry … my reporting appears for tactics for units or functions she is not the custodian or the owner”

1 · The rule

One question, asked per unit or function: do I run this one? — am I its owner, its strategy custodian or its function head.

  • If I run it — I enter everything on that unit’s own Reporting page, tactics included. There is no My reporting tab for it.
  • If I don’t run it but own tactics there — those lines appear on My reporting, and that is where I type them.
  • A line somebody else owns, inside a unit I run — I see the figure, I don’t type it.
  • Figure sets are unchanged — where Finance owns a set of numbers inside my unit, Finance still enters them.
  • The switch stays, off by default. Off, none of this happens.

Two things wrong with that sentence, on both screens

“83 83 lines” — the number is printed twice. One word in the builder: the helper that makes a plural already returns the count and the word, and the count was put in front of it as well.

And 83 is the wrong number. It counts every tactic that names an owner. On the worked example 83 name one and only 51 name somebody who is on the register — the other 32 name a person the platform has never heard of. Neither is fixed here; say the word and both go in one edit.

5 · What it costs, measured on the worked example

83 tactics, every one naming an owner. 51 name somebody on the register.

  • 49 of those 51 are owned by somebody who also runs that unit. Those people lose a second screen and gain nothing else.
  • 2 are owned by somebody who runs nothing there. Those are the only lines that reach My reporting, and they are one person’s.
  • 32 name nobody the platform knows. Today, with the switch on, one person in thirty-three can enter them — the SMO. Under your rule the unit’s owner and its custodian can too.

On a real client with tactics owned across units the middle number will be larger. On the demo the feature is nearly invisible, which is your point measured.

6 · The one judgement call

“Do I run this one?” is asked as can I enter figures for this unit at all — the grant on Roles & access — rather than as a list of the three role names. They agree everywhere on the worked example. They differ in one corner: a custodian whose Reporting cell has been set to view. Asked the first way they get My reporting for their own lines; asked the second way they would get nothing anywhere. I have taken the first. Say if you want the other.
